newsitem.title: UK: IPE natgas mixed, flex market shows prompt strengt.
newsitem.headline: IPE natgas mixed, flex market shows prompt strengt.

text.p: The IPE natural gas futures contract saw little trade and mixed price signals on Monday morning as deals were done both above and below the previous settlement.

July saw five lots trade unchanged at 10.315, while in September five lots traded off by 0.075 pence a therm to 10.415 pence and in March 10 lots rose by 0.005 pence, the minimum tick size, to 14.00 pence.

On the flexibility mechanism there were system buys on both Saturday and Monday, with the system buying around 5 million therms on Saturday and around 7 million on Monday, a dealer said. The System Marginal Price (SMP), the highest price paid, was 0.4003 pence a kilowatt hour on Saturday and 0.4001 p/kWh on Monday, around 11.73 pence a therm in each case, he added.

"Demand is relatively high, it's well supported on prompt and there's not a lot of prompt gas around," a trader said. Day ahead gas on the spot market was discussed between 10.20 and 10.60 pence a therm on Monday morning, while within day gas was heard offered at 11.50 pence.

There was a bid for the 1999 gas year - running from October 1999 to September 2000 - heard at 13.35 pence a therm, with at least one offer of 14.75 pence given in response. But both futures and physical markets were generally quiet, with London's rush hour transport chaos cited as a possible contributing factor.
